image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a male mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The duck is resting with its head tucked back onto its shoulder/back. Visible features include an iridescent green head, a yellow bill, a white neck ring, mottled brown and grey body plumage, and the characteristic curled black tail feathers. The background consists of rippling water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, exhibiting the correct broad, flat shape and yellow-green coloration typical of a mallard drake.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears robust and compact. The plumage texture looks dense and layered, consistent with waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and mottled brown/grey body feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged or occluded by the body and water; they are not visible in this frame.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body. While folded, the structure appears consistent with broad, pointed wings tucked against the flank.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The rear of the duck shows the distinctive upward-curling black central tail feathers, a key identifier for male mallards.

artifact_observations.location: Feather edges on the back/shoulder area

The interaction between the duck's belly and the water is somewhat indistinct. The reflection and displacement of water around the lower body lack sharp physical definition, appearing slightly smeared.
